Source_Title: Combined metabolomics and electronic tongue technology elucidated the mechanisms of regulation of color–taste characteristics of Huangqin (Scutellaria baicalensis Georgi) herbal tea after various roasting processes
Relevant_Targets: Baicalin; other Scutellaria gap analytes checked against published tables
Access_and_Matrix_Assessment: Open-access full text. Table 2 reports baicalin in processed Huangqin herbal tea leaves from five roasting/drying treatments; exact sample preparation and external-standard HPLC method are stated. Source describes HHT as tea/beverage, but table measures ground leaf material, not brewed infusion. mg/g sample denominator is retained; moisture basis and independent HPLC replicate count are not reported in accessible text.
Scientific_Decision: Accept five Baicalin records only. Use Table 2 HPLC column, not the LC-MS peak-area column. Do not infer infusion, fresh-weight, or dry-weight values. No calibrated sample-level values for the other six exact gap analytes were verified in this source.

Source_Title: Widely targeted metabolomics analysis reveals effects of raw material parts, harvest season, and processing technology of Huangqin (Scutellaria baicalensis Georgi) tea
Access_and_Matrix_Assessment: Publisher abstract remains accessible; no full text, supplement, repository dataset, or target-specific calibrated sample values located in this follow-up. Abstract gives comparative trends and states underlying data are available from corresponding author on request.
Scientific_Decision: Keep comparative statements out of quantitative composition. Prepare, but do not send, a data request for baicalin/wogonoside calibration, sample-level values, matrices, and denominators.

Source_Title: Organic Acid-Catalyzed Subcritical Water Hydrolysis of Immature Citrus unshiu Pomace
Source_Classification: Primary analytical measurement; process-generated hydrolysis yield
Access_and_Matrix_Assessment: Open full text; Table 1 provides 13 run-level prunin values from subcritical-water/citric-acid hydrolysates of freeze-dried immature Citrus unshiu pomace. Values are normalized per gram of dry starting pomace; hydrolysis changes the analyte pool and can generate/liberate prunin.
Scientific_Decision: Retain exact table values as held process-yield candidates only. They are not native prunin concentrations in unprocessed edible citrus and are not ingested.

Source_Title: Hesperetin 7-O-glucoside and prunin in Citrus species (C. aurantium and C. paradisi): quantitative distribution in immature fruits
Access_and_Matrix_Assessment: Primary article bibliographic record/abstract is traceable; numerical table and full measurement basis remain inaccessible in this run; no verified repository or supplement copy located.
Scientific_Decision: Keep the 1993 lead unresolved. No value, unit, or basis transcribed from secondary citations.
